tagline.text: A family park on the ridge overlooking Taal Lake and the volcano

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (per person, rough total including admission, activities, and meals)

children.text: Tagaytay Picnic Grove is a park on the Tagaytay ridge with views down to Taal Lake and Volcano Island. You can rent a table or hut for a packed lunch, try a zipline or horseback ride, and walk the viewing trails, making it an easy day trip from Manila.
Tagaytay Picnic Grove is a park beside the ridge road in Tagaytay City, Cavite. Wikipedia describes Tagaytay as a ridge-top city at an average elevation of about

on the rim of the Taal Caldera, with several viewpoints that look out to the volcano island in the middle of the lake. The Picnic Grove is presented as one of the few parks on the ridge from which you can see both the lake and the volcano, and it also marks the end of Ligaya Drive, the winding road that climbs from near Talisay.

The appeal of this park lies in its relaxed pace rather than in grand facilities. You can rent a table or hut in the shade of the trees and eat a packed lunch, do your own grilling in designated areas, and spend the day with family and friends. There are light activities such as a zipline and horseback riding, a tree-top skywalk described as about 500 m long, and an open lawn for kite flying. Some facilities are said to need upgrades, but in recent years a viewing deck and multi-level parking have reportedly been added. Some stretches have slopes and steps, so wear comfortable shoes. Google Maps shows more than 10,000 reviews with a 4.4 rating, a sign of how many people visit. The typical visit is described as 2–3 hours.
Tagaytay is about
59 km
from Manila via Aguinaldo Highway, and its average temperature of about

is cooler than Manila's. From December to February it is known to be foggy, windy, and cooler still. That is why people come on weekends to escape the heat of Manila for a day. Google ratings are in the low fours, and reviews tend to praise the views and the family atmosphere while pointing out that some facilities are aging.

Always check the volcano's status. Taal Volcano is monitored by the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS), and all of Volcano Island is designated a Permanent Danger Zone. You look at the volcano from a safe distance in the park, but if the alert level rises, travel and operations in the area may be affected, so check PHIVOLCS notices and city announcements before you go.

From the park's viewpoints you can see the lake and the volcano island in the middle of it together. Clear mornings give the best views. In the foggy months of December–February visibility can be poor, so check the weather.

blocks.title: Picnic with a table or hut

children.text: You can rent a table, picnic hut, family shed, or pavilion, and you are welcome to bring your own food. Some spots are described as having grilling provisions. 2026 guides list ₱150 for a table up to ₱600 for a pavilion depending on size, so check on site. On weekends the best spots fill early, so it is wise to claim one as soon as you arrive.

The park's zipline is an easy activity for a first try. One guide lists ₱300 for a round trip, while another says ₱200–500 depending on type and day, with weekdays cheaper. Check rates and weight limits on site.

There is a dedicated horseback circuit where you can take a short ride. A recent guide lists ₱350 for 30 minutes while an older one says ₱150–200, so it can vary with time and distance. Ask staff about handling the horse and safety rules first.
A skywalk running among the trees, a viewing deck, and viewpoints in the Picnic Town area are described as newly improved. Walk slowly and look at the lake from several angles.
There is an eco-trail and an open lawn where you can fly a kite or play badminton. It is especially good for families with children.

Inside the park are food stands and a food hub where you can buy snacks or pick up anything you forgot. Menus and prices differ by stall. Tagaytay is known for many restaurants serving bulalo and crispy tawilis from Taal Lake.
There are souvenir shops at the entrance and inside the park. They are good for browsing Tagaytay specialties, but compare prices or negotiate before buying.

items.title: Day trip from Manila
items.subtitle: Morning views and an afternoon picnic

children.text: Leave Manila for Tagaytay by bus or car. Weekend mornings are congested, so set out early.
In central Tagaytay (around the Rotonda), take a Calamba-bound jeepney and get off at Picnic Grove.
Buy your ticket at the entrance and start with the viewpoints, photographing the lake on a clear morning.
Try an activity such as the zipline or a horse ride, and claim a table or hut for lunch.
Have lunch, then walk the skywalk and the eco-trail at an easy pace.
Head to People's Park in the Sky or a café in town, or get ready to go home.
Both the park and the roads are very crowded on weekends. Go on a weekday if you can, and allow for traffic on the way back.
Arrive in Tagaytay early and see the Picnic Grove view first.
After your activities, move into town and have bulalo for lunch.
See the view from another angle at People's Park in the Sky.
Rest at a café or souvenir shop and head home before dark.
The sites are some distance apart, so with a larger group it is easier to hire one vehicle.
Tagaytay is about
59 km
from Manila via Aguinaldo Highway. Buses to Tagaytay run from terminals in Manila. Check companies, schedules, and fares at the terminal.
In central Tagaytay around Olivarez (the Rotonda), board a jeepney bound for Calamba or People's Park and tell the driver to drop you at Picnic Grove. One guide describes this method.
One review says a tricycle from the park to the jeepney stop costs about ₱100.
Weekend traffic into Tagaytay is often heavy, so we recommend leaving early in the morning. Jeepney routes and fares can change, so check locally.
By car you can enter Tagaytay via SLEX and then the Tagaytay–Calamba Road or Aguinaldo Highway. Use a navigation app with live traffic.
Parking is listed at ₱50 for cars, ₱75 for vans, jeepneys, and coasters, ₱150 for buses, and free for motorcycles.
Day tours from Manila to Tagaytay usually gather at places such as SM Mall of Asia. Prices vary by operator.
In Tagaytay town you can use jeepneys, tricycles, and ride-hailing. Confirm the fare before you ride.
Tagaytay is cooler than Manila and pleasant year-round, but in the rainy months of June–October rain and fog can hide the view. Clear mornings in the November–April dry season give the best views.

From December to February fog and wind increase and temperatures drop, which is refreshing, but some days the lake cannot be seen. A weekday morning avoids the crowds, and on weekends and holidays it is best to arrive early.
The Tagaytay ridge runs about
32 km
from Mount Batulao in the west to Mount Sungay in the east, and Mount Sungay, at about

, is the highest point in Cavite. The Picnic Grove is a park that looks down on the lake from this ridge. Visibility varies greatly with the weather, so check the forecast before you leave, and on poor-visibility days shift your plan toward the picnic and the food.

Tagaytay has plenty of places to stay, so it is also a good place to spend the night. There is no lodging in the park itself, so check hotels and resorts in town or along the ridge road on a booking site by date. They fill early on weekends and holidays.

There are two ways to eat. You can bring your own food and eat in a hut, or use the food stands in the park. Tagaytay is known for bulalo (beef shank and marrow soup) and fried tawilis from Taal Lake, so town restaurants are a good place to try them. Opening hours and prices differ by shop.
Taal Lake is a caldera lake of about 234 km², the third largest lake in the Philippines, with a maximum depth of about

. Knowing that the view in front of you is such a huge volcanic lake makes it more impressive. Tawilis, the lake's signature fish, is known as a freshwater sardine found only here, and overharvesting is described as a problem. Check menus and prices when you order it.
A weekday morning is the quietest and gives the clearest view.
Admission and activity rates can change, so check at the entrance.
If you use a table or hut, staff come around to collect the fee, so look at the rate list first.
It is cool here, but the sun is strong in the daytime, so bring a hat and sunscreen.
On rainy days bring a rain jacket or umbrella.
If you bring food, take your trash with you or put it in the designated places.
Check the safety rules with staff before riding a horse or the zipline.
If the parking lot is crowded, do not stop on the nearby road and follow the directions.
If you visit with family, bring snacks for the children, water, and a change of clothes.
Taal is an active volcano, so check the PHIVOLCS alert level and city announcements before you go. If the level rises, travel and facility operations in the area may change.
Rates and opening hours can change, so check just before you visit.
Traffic and parking are very congested on weekends and holidays.
Some facilities in the park may be under repair or aging, so keep your expectations in check.
Access to Volcano Island is restricted depending on the PHIVOLCS alert level, so check the latest notices.
In crowded places, keep a close watch on your belongings and phone.
Another viewpoint park on the Tagaytay ridge, with admission listed at around ₱50. It pairs well with the Picnic Grove.
